text_: I grabbed this for a long flight expecting a dusty old classic, but man, it completely surprised me. For the price of a fancy coffee, you get hundreds of pages of pure adventure, shipwrecks, treehouses, animal taming, the works. It's genuinely exciting and surprisingly practical, like a survival guide wrapped in a family saga. My kids started listening while I read aloud and now they're obsessed. No filler, just solid storytelling that holds up way better than I expected. Honestly, it's a steal if you want something engaging that doesn't require a screen. Zero regrets, and I'll probably reread it next summer.

text_: I went into Betrayed with sky-high expectations after the rest of the series, and somehow Tara still managed to blow them away. This book digs deeper into Dom's world than I ever expected, layers of family history that change everything you thought you knew. The tension between protecting his marriage and confronting old wounds felt so real, not melodramatic at all. I appreciated that Baby V's storyline didn't just coast on the earlier setup; it actually landed in a way that surprised me. The pacing is relentless in the best way, but there are quiet moments that hit just as hard. I finished it in two sittings and immediately wanted to go back and re-read key scenes. If you've been following this series, this is the payoff you've been hoping for.
